extracted.intended_audience: authors and editors preparing or commissioning developmental edits for book-length manuscripts (fiction and nonfiction)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical, page-level checklist and briefing guide for commissioning and running a developmental edit of a book-length manuscript, covering setup, structural and line-level diagnostics, worldbuilding, market positioning, and revision planning for both fiction and nonfiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define your goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick one primary aim and two secondary aims for the edit (examples: structure, character/thesis clarity, pacing, market fit). Write one sentence for each aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a clear brief so every note serves those aims; tape the sentences above your desk; primary/secondary priorities steer editor focus and prevent scatter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a briefing pack
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a short, skimmable pack: 1–2 page synopsis (spoilers included), chapter outline (one line per chapter), cast or key concepts, short author bio, and a mini exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reverse outline (chapter purpose/conflict/change), list of main characters with roles/wants/ages (or core concepts for nonfiction), publishing goal (trade/self), and a 300-word fast-book exercise to reveal gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify audience and comps
rubrics_metrics.description: Name the primary reader in one line (age range, interests, expected benefit) and pick 3–5 comparable recent titles; for each comp, state what readers expect and how your book delivers/differs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finish the sentence: 'Readers who loved [Title] will expect [feature]. My book delivers [feature] and differs in [one meaningful way].' Use examples for fiction and nonfiction to align tone/structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Define non-negotiables and limits: target word count by genre, must-keep elements, deal-breakers (tone/content), timeline, and publishing path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write these on the first page of the pack. Examples: genre-specific word-count ranges, required dual timeline, topics to avoid, revision timelines, and whether the book targets trade or self-publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare working files
rubrics_metrics.description: Format the manuscript for easy markup and consistent editorial work: .docx single file, chapter breaks on new pages, 12 pt, double-spaced, page numbers, clear scene breaks, and Word styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable Track Changes/comments, mark scene breaks (e.g., # on a blank line), start a one-page style sheet (names, invented terms, hyphenation, numbers, spelling choice, formatting rules) and update it during revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write the right questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick five big, focused editorial questions (not line edits) that guide the edit and one open slot for surprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiction examples: 'Where does the story sag?' 'Does the protagonist drive the plot through choices?' Nonfiction examples: 'Is the thesis simple and bold?' 'Does each chapter advance the argument?' Use the questions to focus notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide scope and follow-ups
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree the level of review (full manuscript vs partial), deliverables (editorial letter, margin notes), meetings (kick-off, debrief), recheck terms, and timelines before work begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A partial (e.g., first 50 pages + synopsis) suits early structure checks; full reviews for mature drafts. Define whether margin notes accompany the letter and whether a short recheck is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample request message
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate succinctly when requesting an edit: title, genre, word count, aims, included materials, deliverables desired, timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a sample template that sets expectations for availability, quote, and deliverables; clear upfront scope reduces surprises and scope creep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Name the book's promise in one sentence: premise/thesis plus the change or outcome a reader expects (fiction and nonfiction templates provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiction template: 'A [character] must [goal] before [ticking threat], or [cost].' Nonfiction template: 'This book helps [reader] achieve [outcome] by [method].' Test the promise on a friend for clarity and appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify major beats and the chain between them (for fiction: inciting incident, midpoint reversal, crisis, climax, resolution; for nonfiction: logical table of contents and progressive learning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure scenes trigger one another (causality), write a one-line beat sheet (five lines for fiction, one per chapter for nonfiction), and fix gaps before line-level polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Throughlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Track and maintain throughlines that run through the book: protagonist goal, motivation, conflict, alignment of character change and plot events, and subplots that support the main story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a quick grid/color-coding to mark central goal/thesis and subplots; cut or fold subplots that do not pressure the central story; ensure nonfiction chapters advance the thesis and place evidence where readers need it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakes and escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure every turn raises consequences; escalation should come from choices rather than random events, and setups must pay off before the finale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fiction, escalate personal/social/public stakes and ensure reversals arise from choices. For nonfiction, each chapter should introduce a tougher question and scale examples from simple to complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistent chronology: track dates, times, seasons, scene durations, ages, and dependencies to avoid time-based inconsistencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a dated scene list, a calendar for the book's period, an age/milestones chart; spot-check travel math, injuries/healing windows, academic/fiscal calendars, and tech availability for the period/place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundancy audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit the manuscript for repeated beats, scenes, or arguments; combine, cut, or move material so each beat earns its place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print a list of scenes/sections and note each purpose in five words or fewer; merge duplicate scenes, remove repeated characterization, and set reduction targets (e.g., reduce by 8,000 words) starting with repeats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open issues list
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a running list of plot holes, unanswered questions, missing bridges, research gaps, permissions, and items to fix/park with owners and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark items as fix now, research, or park for later; finish the structural pass with a one-line promise, a beat sheet/TOC with objectives, and a short issues list with owners and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene purpose check
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that every scene or chapter has three elements: a goal, friction (obstacle), and a change (win/loss or new knowledge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate margins with G, F, C for each scene; blank boxes signal cuts or rewrites. Examples provided for both fiction (steal the file) and nonfiction (teach a method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrances and exits
rubrics_metrics.description: Start scenes late and leave early; open in mid-action/mid-thought/mid-argument and end with either resolution of the beat or a hook forwarding the next scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delete irrelevant arrivals (parking, coffee); ensure nonfiction opens with a question/result/number; test first and last lines of each unit for motion or forward pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposition control
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid info-dumps by delivering background in bite-sized pieces when the reader needs context; prefer action/dialogue for facts that shape choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scan for paragraphs with more than three sentences of pure information and halve them; move some material later or use summary sparingly as a bridge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microtension
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep small, page-level tension (a question, mismatch, deadline, or withheld detail) to pull the reader forward even in quiet scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a microtension device to every page: a question in narration, contrast between words/body language, or a small withheld detail that pays off within a scene; in nonfiction, pose a test or counterexample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary scene/chapter length and mode (dialogue/action/reflection/summary) to avoid monotony and maintain engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate short and long scenes, mix modes, chart word counts for scenes and avoid long runs of the same size; adjust by trimming, splitting, or merging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Signal shifts in time, place, topic, or POV with bridges so handoffs feel smooth and oriented rather than jarring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End scenes with cause that implies the next location, open with time anchors (e.g., 'Friday, sunrise'), state names for POV shifts, and write one-line bridges like 'Because X, we move to Y.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Format text to aid skimming and resuming: short paragraphs, regular subheads, bulleted lists, figures/tables for data, and white space around dense material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot-check random pages for walls of text; add subheads, pull quotes, summary boxes, and one-minute action steps for nonfiction/commuter audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protagonist agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the lead has a clear desire, meaningful obstacles, and consequential choices rather than passive reactions or luck-based fixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name desire in one sentence, list three decisions the lead makes in the first third (if two are reactions, redesign), and avoid deus ex machina solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antagonistic forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Define opposing forces (person, system, or self) with plausible motives so opposition feels real and shapes the protagonist's choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the antagonist 'a day in court'—a paragraph from their view and an early action that reveals intent; ensure systemic antagonists have logic (policy, economics) and self-antagonism links to a wound or flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cast design
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign every named character a clear function/role and a sliver of change; avoid duplicate roles and tokenization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use index cards for name/function/growth beat; merge or drop characters with overlapping functions; for nonfiction, treat concepts/sources as cast members with unique functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: POV strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose viewpoint (first, close third, distant third, second), tense, and psychic distance and consistently honor that contract with rules for shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One viewpoint per scene, signal time jumps early, map rotation for multi-POV books, and audit for leaked thought words crossing heads (knew, wondered, noticed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interiority and dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Blend thought, feeling, and action so internality serves decisions; craft dialogue to carry subtext and push change rather than recap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pages of rumination without action; use body language over tags; replace on-the-nose explanatory speech with visible action or objects that show backstory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a consistent voice (vocabulary, sentence length, stance) suited to the audience and avoid clichés, mixed metaphors, and inconsistent moral posture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test by reading pages aloud for rhythm variety; maintain stance (dry, wry, urgent, calm), set profanity/slang limits in the mini style sheet, and use jargon with definition and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether you are an expert, guide, or peer and honor the boundaries of that role (citations, methods, limits, empathy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts lead with evidence and boundaries; guides show steps, mistakes, and expected effort; peers share experience and options. Use disclaimers for health/legal/financial topics and cite sources or refer to professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character/POV/Voice quick diagnostic checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: A short checklist verifying lead agency, opposing forces, supporting roles, POV consistency, interplay of thoughts/dialogue, and voice suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist as a pass: does the lead drive action via costs/choices; do opposing forces have credible motives; is POV steady; do thoughts/dialogue move scenes; does voice match reader expectations?

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of the world
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly define core rules/constraints of the story world (magic, tech, legal), show costs for breaking rules, and place consequences on the page before the midpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List three core rules with one visible cost, one loophole, and one consequence; ensure rules are visible and respected or their subversion is believable and costly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting as function
rubrics_metrics.description: Use place and sensory detail to shape choices and mood; settings should affect decisions, not just decorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut generic weather; pick telling objects; use locations (warehouse walkthrough vs theory paragraph) to teach or advance plot; write two lines showing how setting blocks the easy path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity bible
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a single-reference bible (spreadsheet/tab) tracking items: Item, First seen, Description/rule, Later reference, Status, plus a dated timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track names, spellings, ages, units, streets, moon phases, travel times, and season markers; highlight every number in the draft and verify sources or logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use original sources, record full citation metadata, log permissions for quotes/epigraphs, and flag uncertainties (TK) in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find two independent sources for statistics, record title/author/URL/access date, keep a permissions list for copyrighted material, and qualify or drop claims if methods are weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Portray people as full humans rather than props; show diversity of views within groups and avoid caricature or phonetic accents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hire/pay sensitivity readers with relevant expertise, anonymize case-study details when needed, get consent for risky stories, and provide context for historical/cultural practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausibility checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify intersections with the real world: travel logistics, medical recovery times, legal/procedural accuracy, professional constraints, and timelines for long arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create quick rows (time, distance, money, medicine, law) and note plausibility for each major beat; where wobble occurs, research, insert a workaround, or change the beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify libel/privacy risks, professional advice liabilities, dangerous how-to content, permissions/release needs, and consult experts or lawyers where stakes are high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change identifying details where needed, include disclaimers for medical/legal/financial advice, avoid step-by-step harmful instructions, and store signed releases for interviews/photos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldbuilding quick diagnostic checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist verifying that rules have costs, setting shapes choices, a bible tracks continuity, sources are vetted, representation is deep, and real-world constraints align.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consequences of rule-breaking appear on-page, use a continuity table and timeline, run sensitivity reads, and consult experts for high-risk factual areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Know and map the core promises and must-haves of your category (examples include romance, thriller, fantasy, memoir, business/self-help) and ensure your manuscript delivers or signals deliberate deviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List three must-haves per category, tag scenes/chapters that provide them, and signal any intentional deviations early in text or jacket copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count check
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare manuscript word count to category norms and plan cuts or expansions accordingly (examples: romance 70–90k, thrillers 60–80k, epic fantasy 90–120k, nonfiction 50–75k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write current total on a sticky note, trim when over the mark, add beats when far below to meet shelf expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique value proposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate in one breath why a reader would choose this book—emotional payoff for fiction or specific outcomes for nonfiction using provided templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hook templates (fiction and nonfiction) and test the hook on a friend for clarity about genre, tone, and stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Map 3–5 comparable recent titles, note alignments and differences, and use that analysis to adjust structure, tone, or content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write two sentences per comp (what aligns, where you differ); adjust your manuscript to fill gaps or better match reader expectations when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader journey
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure readers experience a satisfying arc: promise early, escalation mid, a decision near the end, and an emotional or skill-based payoff appropriate to genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonfiction ensure recaps/exercises/checklists where helpful; do a five-minute audit by listing the first/last sentence of each chapter to confirm build rather than wobble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut and expand decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Triage material into Keep & polish, Deepen, Merge, or Cut, and plan bridge work to sew payoffs and foreshadowing where needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List three foreshadowing seeds for major payoffs, add echoes of the core motif every few chapters, and provide sample entries (chapter-level notes) for practical edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritised to-do list
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort revision tasks by impact (structure, character/argument, pacing, prose) and track Task/Driver/Scope/Owner/Date in a simple tracker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus big rocks first; run short sprints (e.g., two structural changes + two deepens) and hold weekly reviews to adjust scope. Use color/letters if helpful for triage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Next steps / beta readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring in early readers after major structural choices settle; brief beta readers with the hook, target reader, and three focus questions (no line edits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collate patterns from beta feedback and ignore single outliers unless they match your instincts; run one more developmental pass before line/copy editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare query materials aligned to the current draft: fiction query (hook, mini-synopsis, bio), synopsis (1–2 pages chronological), and nonfiction proposal (overview, market, bio, chapter outcomes, sample chapters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update pitch after major revisions: sharpen hook, align chapter summaries to revised order, and ensure word count is accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market fit quick diagnostic checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: A checklist to confirm genre promises appear on the page, hooks/stakes are clear, comps support positioning, reader journey builds to payoff, and submission materials reflect the current version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm to-do lists exist that prioritize structure and argument before prose, beta readers are briefed with focus questions, and query/proposal materials match the revised manuscript.
